Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Nature & food

produce verb

of land and plants: yield

also yield, bear fruit, bring forth

classical

Cic. Leg. 2.67: quae autem terra frūgēs ferre … possit
Ov. Met. 1.109: frūgēs tellūs inarāta ferēbat

ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum

verb, irregular

bear, yield (of land, trees, a country)

The land or the tree is the subject: ager frūmentum fert; a fertile field is ferāx. Of people making goods, Latin says facere (see make).

Other words

  • efferō, efferre, extulī, ēlātum — bring forth, yield (of land)

    verb, irregular · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.48: agrōs fertilēs, quī multō plūs efferunt quam accēpērunt

  • gignō, gignere, genuī, genitum — produce (of a land, the sea, nature)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 12.6: gignit et Ōceanus margarīta; Sen. Ep. 18.14: immodica īra gignit īnsāniam

  • pariō, parere, peperī, partum — bring forth, produce

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. N. D. 1.4: frūgēs et reliqua, quae terra pariat; Ov. Ars 1.757: nec tellūs eadem parit omnia

    Properly of giving birth; also of the earth bringing forth crops.

Examples

  • mox etiam frūgēs tellūs inarāta ferēbat

    soon the earth, unploughed, produced crops as wellOv. Met. 1.109

  • an imitārī agrōs fertilēs, quī multō plūs efferunt quam accēpērunt?

    or should we copy fertile fields, which produce far more than they received?Cic. Off. 1.48

  • nec tellūs eadem parit omnia; vītibus illa convenit, haec oleīs; hāc bene farra virent

    nor does the same soil produce everything: one suits vines, another olives; in this one the wheat grows greenOv. Ars 1.757–758

See also produce, produce, make, harvest.
